decisions.basis: NL5 requirement quote 'where the cooking time is displayed and updated' from llms_emp_feedback_final_0055.puml:line:13; FCSTM state:ReadytoCook:line:15 with empty abstract_action_inventory from inspection_equivalent_facts; candidate basis confirming no action annotation in model text.
decisions.reason: NL5 explicitly attaches 'the cooking time is displayed and updated' to the ReadytoCook state using the standard UML in-state behavior pattern ('where [behavior]'). The closed FCSTM model declares state ReadytoCook at line 15 with no associated actions. The reference inspection facts confirm abstract_action_inventory is empty and no variable or action dataflow exists. The 'descriptive gloss' alternative is not a competent reading because the NL structure 'state X, where [specific data operation]' is the standard UML do-activity specification pattern, not mere description. The model's complete absence of any action on this state confirms the gap.
decisions.violated_obligation: The ReadytoCook state should carry a do-activity that displays and updates the cooking time, per NL5's 'where the cooking time is displayed and updated'.

decisions.basis: NL6 requirement quote 'canceling or updating the cooking time' from llms_emp_feedback_final_0055.puml:line:18; FCSTM transition:line:27 with effects=[] from inspection_equivalent_facts; candidate basis confirming no effect annotation in model text.
decisions.reason: NL6 states 'the system returns to DoorShutWithItem, canceling or updating the cooking time.' The participial clause is syntactically attached to the transition, specifying a required effect. The closed FCSTM transition at line 27 (ReadytoCook -> DoorShutWithItem : /Cancel) has effects=[] and guard=null, confirmed by inspection_equivalent_facts. The 'semantic consequence of returning' alternative is not competent because the NL structures the cancel/update as a parallel action to the state change (both consequences of the Cancel event), not as a consequence of the state change itself. The model's empty effects field confirms the gap.
decisions.violated_obligation: The transition from ReadytoCook to DoorShutWithItem triggered by Cancel should carry an effect that cancels or updates the cooking time, per NL6's participial clause.

decisions.basis: NL8 requirement quote 'if the timer expires, the system moves to DoorShutWithItem' from llms_emp_feedback_final_0055.puml:line:23; precise binding of transition:line:31 connecting state:Cooking:line:16 on event:Timer_Expired:line:10 to state:DoorShutWithItem:line:14 in the closed FCSTM model.

The 'observed' field notes that runtime confirmation is delegated, but the exact structural binding already satisfies the expected property: the post-stimulus state per the model's transition topology IS DoorShutWithItem. issues.requirement_quote: canceling or updating the cooking time
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The phrase 'canceling or updating the cooking time' could be interpreted as a natural-language description of the semantic consequence of returning to DoorShutWithItem rather than a formally required UML effect; however, the NL attaches it as a participial clause directly to the transition event, and the contract extraction typed it as an independent effect obligation.
issues.title: Cancel transition from ReadytoCook to DoorShutWithItem lacks required cancel-or-update cooking time effect

issues.basis: NL7 text: 'the system transitions to the Cooking state, where the timer starts'; FCSTM line 16: 'state Cooking named "Cooking"' with no action annotation; inspection_equivalent_facts: abstract_action_inventory=[].
issues.expected: The Cooking state should carry a do-activity that starts the timer.
issues.observed: The closed FCSTM model declares state Cooking at line 16 with no associated actions, do-activities, or effects. The reference inspection facts confirm abstract_action_inventory is empty and no variable dataflow exists.
issues.reason: NL7 explicitly requires that in the Cooking state, 'the timer starts.' The closed model has no action or do-activity on this state. No phase hint is supplied, so S4 cannot be applied; the precise gap is preserved as predicate-null W1.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The NL phrasing 'where the timer starts' could be read as describing the entry semantics of Cooking rather than a continuous do-activity; however, no explicit lifecycle phase (entry, do, exit) is stated in the NL, and the contract binding hints contain no phase value, so the obligation remains a state_action without S4 eligibility.
issues.title: Cooking state lacks required timer-starts action

issues.basis: NL8 text: 'In the Cooking state, opening the door stops the timer and the system transitions to DoorOpenWithItem'; FCSTM line 30: 'Cooking -> DoorOpenWithItem : /Door_Opened' with no effect; inspection_equivalent_facts transition:line:30 shows effects=[].
issues.expected: The transition from Cooking to DoorOpenWithItem triggered by door opened should carry an effect that stops the timer.
issues.observed: The closed FCSTM transition at line 30 (Cooking -> DoorOpenWithItem : /Door_Opened) has effects=[] and guard=null. No effect annotation is present in the model text or in the inspection-equivalent facts.
issues.reason: NL8 states that 'opening the door stops the timer and the system transitions to DoorOpenWithItem.' The closed model's carrier transition (line 30) has no effect field populated. No frozen predicate directly checks transition effects, so this is preserved as predicate-null W1.
issues.requirement_quote: opening the door stops the timer
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The effect 'stops the timer' could be interpreted as an implicit semantic consequence of exiting the Cooking state rather than a formally required UML effect; however, the NL explicitly states 'opening the door stops the timer' as a distinct causal clause attached to the specific door-opened transition from Cooking.
issues.title: Door-opened transition from Cooking to DoorOpenWithItem lacks required stop-timer effect

The NL describes a flat state machine with six states (DoorShut, DoorOpen, DoorOpenWithItem, DoorShutWithItem, ReadytoCook, Cooking) and no explicit composite/nested hierarchy, so no separate containment contracts are warranted. All transition endpoints, triggers, guards, effects, and state actions are captured. No segment establishes an explicit termination/completion state, event-consumer coverage requirement, deadlock-freedom obligation, state-retention requirement, guard-disjointness requirement (alternatives are already distinguished by different events), or excess-behavior prohibition. The two state-action clauses ("where the cooking time is displayed and updated" in NL5 and "where the timer starts" in NL7) are correctly represented without invented lifecycle phases. The effect contracts for timer-stopping (NL8) and cooking-time-canceling/updating (NL6) are present. All transition groups preserve their complete alternative sets with correct event and guard projections.
